title: Focus ring & micro-interaction accessibility notes — wireframes + backlog
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note from the console UX / DS sync. Focus: small-but-high-impact accessibility improvements around keyboard focus, micro-interaction timing, and their representation in wireframes/components. Goal is to create a minimal set of token conventions + implementation guidance so engineering can ship consistent, accessible behavior across routes and tool panels.

Context / motivation:
- Multiple recent bug reports about keyboard focus 'losing' position after async content loads (search, model catalog).
- Inconsistent focus ring styles across components (table rows, chip list, secondary buttons).
- Motion and hover timing differences create surprising behavior for keyboard users and screen reader users when focus triggers tooltips or flyouts.
- We want a small set of tokens + recommended ARIA patterns to reduce regressions and make QA reproducible.

Key observations from current wireframes / prototypes:
- Floating panels (right rail) often auto-focus first tabbable element; sometimes focus moves to hidden inputs during animation.
- Buttons use 2 different focus outlines: thin blue 1px vs thick 3px in other places. No single token.
- Tooltips are triggered on hover after 120ms, on focus immediately. Keyboard users experience immediate tooltip + live region announcement while pointer users see a delay -> inconsistent UX.
- 'Dismiss' X icons are visually small (18px) and lack an expanded hit target or visible focus state in low-contrast themes.

Proposed tokens (minimal set to standardize):
- --rdw-focus-outline-color: rgb(28, 115, 238)
- --rdw-focus-outline-width: 3px
- --rdw-focus-offset: 2px /* gap between element edge and outline */
- --rdw-focus-ring-radius: 6px
- --rdw-motion-duration-sm: 120ms
- --rdw-motion-duration-md: 240ms
- --rdw-tooltip-delay-pointer: 200ms
- --rdw-tooltip-delay-keyboard: 0ms
- --rdw-hit-target-min: 44px /* ensure small icons meet minimum touch target */
- --rdw-high-contrast-focus: 4px solid WindowText /* for forced high-contrast mode */

Behavioral rules (implementation guidance):
1) Focus preservation during async updates
   - When a component triggers an async refresh that would re-render the focused element, capture a stable identifier (data-focus-id) and restore focus after render.
   - If the element is removed, shift focus to a sensible fallback (next tabbable within the same landmark) and announce via aria-live polite: "(item name) removed, focus moved to (section)".
2) Focus ring and visible focus
   - Use --rdw-focus-outline-* tokens for all focusable primitives (buttons, links, inputs, chips, table rows) so visually consistent.
   - Provide a focus-visible polyfill for browsers without :focus-visible; fallback to :focus but only show outline if keyboard input detected.
3) Tooltips & flyouts
   - Pointer hover: delay = --rdw-tooltip-delay-pointer (200ms).
   - Keyboard focus: delay = --rdw-tooltip-delay-keyboard (0ms) and tooltip content should be accessible via aria-describedby.
   - Do not auto-shift focus into flyouts on hover; only move focus on explicit keyboard interactions (Enter/Space) or click.
4) Motion reduction
   - Respect prefers-reduced-motion. Reduce all nonessential transitions to 0ms and prefer instant state changes for users who signal reduced motion.
5) Small icons & hit targets
   - Ensure interactive icons (close, clear) expand to --rdw-hit-target-min using padding or an invisible focusable wrapper. Show visual focus within expanded area.

Wireframe-specific notes (attached frames referred by id):
- Right rail settings (frame rr-06): initial focus should be on the header-level h2 so screen readers hear context; the first interactive control must not steal focus during slide-in animation. Add aria-live region we can toggle for async status messages.
- Model card grid (frame grid-01): when cards are keyboard-navigated, press Enter opens the card but focus must move to modal header (not the first button) to preserve context. Table-based keyboard navigation is preferred for dense lists.
- Route list (frame routes-09): rows are clickable + focusable. On keyboard focus, show outline and secondary action buttons appear. Avoid keyboard-triggered hover-only reveals; secondary actions must be tabbable.

Accessibility test cases (QA checklist):
- Keyboard traversal: tab order, focus visibility, and focus restoration after async updates. Steps: 1) Tab to interactive element; 2) Trigger async update; 3) Ensure focus restored to identity or moved to fallback with announcement.
- Screen reader check: NVDA + VoiceOver: ensure announcements for additions/removals use polite live regions and do not interrupt. Modal open sequence reads header first.
- Contrast: focus ring must reach 3:1 contrast ratio against background per WCAG AA non-text requirement. Verify high-contrast mode separately.
- Reduced motion: toggle OS reduced-motion and verify no 200+ms animations remain.
- Touch target check: on iOS Safari and mobile Chrome ensure all interactive icons meet 44px min.

Backlog grooming (priority + estimate):
- P0 (1 sprint): focus token implementation across core primitives, focus restoration pattern, small icon hit-target fix. Estimate: 5 dev days + 2 QA days.
- P1 (next sprint): tooltip delay parity and aria-describedby wiring, prefers-reduced-motion handling, focus-visible polyfill. Estimate: 6 dev days.
- P2 (stretch): review and harmonize table-row focus behavior across data-table variants, provide design-kit components for expanded hit-target wrappers. Estimate: 8 dev days.

Acceptance criteria (for each ticket):
- Token exists and is used by component (CSS variable or design token entry).
- Focus behavior has automated unit or integration test (jest + puppeteer/nightwatch test for focus restoration).
- Manual A11y checklist signed off by eng-sre or accessibility reviewer.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Do we prefer a single global focus ring token or separate tokens for "primary focus" vs "element highlight"? (Tradeoff: single token is consistent; separate tokens allow semantic emphasis).
- Should tooltip behavior differ between dense lists and forms? Might be confusing to maintain two delays.
- How to handle 3rd-party embed components (OSS tables) that don't expose focus hooks? Workaround: wrapper that traps focus and proxies events, but adds complexity.

Action items (owners + due):
- Priya: produce a tiny code sandbox demonstrating tokens + focus restoration pattern (due 2026-05-18).
- Ethan: spike an automated focus-restoration test and add to CI (due 2026-05-22).
- Marisol: update console design token page + draft examples (due 2026-05-20).
- Devon: open JIRA tickets per backlog items and link implementation PR (due 2026-05-15).

References and inspiration:
- WAI-ARIA authoring practices (dialog, live region examples)
- Chromium accessibility bug threads on focus after reflow
- Apple HIG guidance on reduced motion and focus indicators

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive on a few small things so we can avoid inconsistent ad-hoc fixes. Ask: what will block shipping? If tokens and focus restoration look good in the sandbox, we should roll out incrementally (buttons/input first, then lists).

Appendix: quick CSS snippets (for engineering):
- Focus CSS (example):
  .rdw-focusable:focus {
    outline: var(--rdw-focus-outline-width) solid var(--rdw-focus-outline-color);
    outline-offset: var(--rdw-focus-offset);
    border-radius: var(--rdw-focus-ring-radius);
  }

- Hit target wrapper (example):
  .icon-button {
    padding: 8px; /* ensure visual spacing */
    min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px;
    display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;
  }

End of notes.
